title: Approve a sarcopenia drug that improves strength and physical function

concept.text: Treat age-related sarcopenia with a medicine that improves patients' functional ability, rather than muscle mass alone. Bimagrumab increased lean mass in a randomized trial but did not significantly improve its primary physical-performance endpoint. Proposed completion test: FDA or EMA approval specifically for sarcopenia, following a pivotal randomized trial in consensus-defined patients showing a clinically meaningful improvement in strength and mobility or disability over at least 12 months. Test set by: Regulators would set approval requirements. EWGSOP2 supplies a diagnostic framework emphasizing low strength, confirmation by low muscle quantity/quality, and physical performance for severity; the 12-month duration is editorial. Overlaps: ORT-06, PHA-09, LON-03. Sources given: [EWGSOP2 consensus definition](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/mid/EMS80409/) ; [Randomized bimagrumab trial in sarcopenia](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2771858).

page.title: Pharmacotherapy for age-related sarcopenia
page.definition: A medicine approved by FDA for age-related sarcopenia would improve or preserve physical function, such as the ability to walk. The revised European consensus calls sarcopenia age-related when aging is the only evident cause. Under those criteria, low muscle strength indicates probable sarcopenia, and low muscle quantity or quality confirms the diagnosis.

goal.need: In one cohort of 1,420 adults aged 75 or older living in the community, 150 had sarcopenia and 85 of them had low physical performance. Exercise can improve strength and function, but some people cannot take part or gain too little benefit. Nutritional supplements have inconsistent effects. A medicine that preserves mobility could help people keep walking across a room or rising from a chair unaided. Gaining lean body mass alone does not establish that benefit.

figures.caption: Changes after six months in the randomized bimagrumab trial
figures.note: Bimagrumab 700 mg monthly: 113 participants; placebo: 67. Values are mean changes. The performance battery assesses balance, walking and chair rises.

statements.quote: During the first half of 2026, Biophytis continued the development of BIO101 (20-hydroxyecdysone), primarily for the sarcopenia and obesity indications.
advancing the development of safe and effective treatment options for managing sarcopenia

completion.title: FDA approves a medicine to treat age-related sarcopenia on evidence of functional benefit.
completion.criterion: FDA issues marketing approval and prescribing information explicitly indicating a medicine for treating age-related sarcopenia, with clinical benefit in patients' physical function supporting the indication. FDA determines that the medicine is safe and effective for this intended use. The approval letter and prescribing information provide the verification record.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, general marketing-approval standard described in Step 4: FDA Drug Review; no sarcopenia-specific numerical approval standard was located.
completion.threshold_quote: safe and effective for its intended use
completion.basis: FDA adjudicates safety and effectiveness for the indication in the approved prescribing information. For this breakthrough, the indication is age-related sarcopenia and the clinical benefit is improved or preserved physical function. ESCEO’s proposed phase III endpoints and 12-month minimum describe a society-recommended trial design. FDA’s general approval standard specifies no sarcopenia endpoint, effect size or trial duration.

milestones.title: A sarcopenia candidate demonstrates pharmacological activity in laboratory studies.
milestones.criterion: Preclinical studies demonstrate pharmacological activity relevant to treating sarcopenia that justifies further development. Safety for initial human exposure requires a separate assessment.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions, preclinical pharmacological-activity criterion; this is a general development criterion, not a sarcopenia-specific effect-size threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: if the compound exhibits pharmacological activity that justifies commercial development.

milestones.title: A sarcopenia candidate completes phase I testing without unacceptable toxicity.
milestones.criterion: Phase I testing characterizes the candidate’s tolerability and dosing in humans without revealing toxicity that would preclude phase II testing.
milestones.set_by: FDA, The FDA's Drug Review Process: Ensuring Drugs Are Safe and Effective, transition from phase I to phase II.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 2 studies begin if Phase 1 studies don't reveal unacceptable toxicity.

milestones.title: SARA-INT shows a gain of at least 0.10 m/s over placebo in usual 400-m walking speed.
milestones.criterion: In SARA-INT participants aged 65 or older with age-related sarcopenia and at risk of mobility disability, compare each BIO101 dose with placebo in the full analysis set. The difference between groups in mean change from baseline in usual walking speed over 400 m must favour BIO101 by at least 0.10 m/s at the protocol’s month-six or month-nine endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Biophytis S.A., SARA-INT protocol BIO101-CL03, version 1.2.11, 20 April 2020, sections 3 and 9.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: A minimum clinically significant benefit is set at 0.1 m/s in the mean difference between groups.

milestones.title: A phase III trial lasting at least 12 months meets physical-performance and patient-reported endpoints.
milestones.criterion: In ambulatory adults aged at least 70 with low muscle strength and low physical performance, a randomized, double-blind trial compares the medicine with placebo alongside standard care. Treatment and follow-up last at least 12 months. The trial meets both prespecified co-primary efficacy criteria, one for physical performance and one for a patient-reported outcome. ESCEO recommends the incidence of becoming unable to complete a 400-m walk as the performance measure and allows alternatives.
milestones.set_by: European Society for Clinical and Economic Aspects of Osteoporosis, Osteoarthritis and Musculoskeletal Diseases, 2020 update of its sarcopenia drug-trial recommendations; these are society recommendations.
milestones.threshold_quote: co-primary endpoints, combining a measure of physical performance with a Patient Reported Outcome Measure (PROM).

milestones.title: FDA accepts a marketing application for an age-related sarcopenia indication for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA determines that the marketing application seeking the age-related sarcopenia indication is sufficiently complete for substantive review and files it. For an original new drug application or biologics license application, FDA makes the filing decision within 60 days of receipt.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, FY 2026 Real Time Report, filing standard for drug and biologics applications.
milestones.threshold_quote: FDA files only applications that are sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

not_found: Searches of FDA and EMA guidance and approval pages found no sarcopenia-specific numerical efficacy threshold for marketing approval.
No published regulatory requirement for both strength and physical function as sarcopenia co-primary endpoints was located.
No successful phase III sarcopenia drug trial meeting the ESCEO co-primary framework was located.

results.finding: BIO101: in a 156-person per-protocol population, the observed 400-m walking-speed difference versus placebo at month 6 was 0.102 m/s.
results.detail: The observed month-6 estimate meets the magnitude threshold. The number with observed data is not stated. The reported primary analysis combined months 6 and 9 and estimated 0.09 m/s in the per-protocol population; 55% of end-of-treatment on-site assessments were lost.
results.quote: In the PP population, the observed difference between treatment arms and placebo was −0.019 and 0.102 m/s for 175 and 350 mg BIO101, respectively, at M6 and 0.019 and 0.078 m/s for 175 and 350 mg BIO101, respectively, at M6/M9 (Figure  S1 ).

results.finding: BIO101 increased C2C12 myotube diameter by 26% versus control across nine independent experiments.
results.quote: After 2 days of treatment with BIO101 (5 μM), a significant (+ 26%;  P  < 0.001) increase in myotube diameter was observed compared with control conditions (Figure  1A ).

results.finding: MF-300 increased maximal plantar-flexor force by 20% versus vehicle in aged male mice (sample size unspecified for this comparison).
results.detail: Dosing was every other day. The conference slides label the results unpublished.

results.finding: Phase I MF-300 cohorts (n=30) showed urinary PGE-MUM reduction during a 5-day dosing study.
results.detail: The slides give no adverse-event or dose-limiting toxicity results.
results.quote: Magnitude of PGE-MUM reduction in human is comparable to reduction coincident with efficacy in aged mice

results.finding: Bimagrumab was generally well tolerated in phase I, with 84 of 91 randomized older adults completing the study.
results.detail: The trial enrolled healthy older adults, a population consistent with the criterion's requirement for human dosing and tolerability assessment.
results.quote: Bimagrumab was generally safe and well tolerated; adverse events were mostly mild to moderate in severity.

results.finding: BIO101 phase I (n=54 across both parts) reported 0 serious adverse events.
results.detail: The study tested single oral doses up to 1,400 mg and repeat doses up to 450 mg twice daily. The investigators selected 350 mg twice daily as the highest SARA-INT dose.
results.quote: No deaths, SAEs or treatment emergent AEs (TEAEs) leading to treatment discontinuation were reported during the study.

results.finding: MF-300 increased muscle force by about 20% across two aged-mouse studies. Animal counts were unreported.
results.detail: The conference presentation attributes the preclinical results to Epirium data on file.
results.quote:
Treatment of naturally aged mice 
with MF-300 for 12 weeks 
demonstrates:
– A ~50% reduction in PGE-MUM 
consistent with target 
engagement 
– Significantly increases muscle 
force by ~20%

results.finding: In phase I testing of MF-300, 88 adults enrolled and 0 dose-limiting toxicities were reported.
results.detail: The older cohorts received a single 125 mg dose or 200 mg once daily for five days. The 800 mg single-dose maximum applied to the younger cohorts.

results.finding: SARA-INT BIO101 (full analysis set, n=232): the higher dose gained 0.039 m/s over placebo in the primary month 6/9 analysis.
results.detail: The observed month-six difference at the higher dose was +0.086 m/s in the full analysis set. The +0.102 m/s estimate came from the per-protocol population. COVID-19 disruptions led to loss of 55% of on-site end-of-treatment efficacy assessments.
results.quote: In the primary analysis of 400MWT GS in the FAS, the least square (LS) mean (SE) difference to placebo in change from baseline to Month 6/9 was 0.036 (0.031) m/s and 0.039 (0.030) m/s in the 175‐and 350‐mg BIO101 groups, respectively

results.finding: RJx-01 produced 32% higher grip strength in aged wild-type mice (6 treated, 10 untreated controls).
results.quote: Mice treated with RJx-01 showed a 32% increase in grip strength compared with the control group

results.finding: SW033291 increased treadmill time to exhaustion versus vehicle in aged mice (n=4 per group) after 1 month of daily treatment.
results.detail: Deleting EP4 in aged myofibers abolished the gains in muscle mass and strength after SW033291 treatment, supporting a PGE2–EP4 mechanism.
results.quote:
Notably, for both young and aged mice endurance (time to 
exhaustion on a treadmill) was significantly increased, suggestive of an overall systemic 
beneficial effect in addition to muscle strength (Fig. 2M).

definition = "A medicine approved by FDA for age-related sarcopenia would improve or preserve physical function, such as the ability to walk. The revised European consensus calls sarcopenia age-related when aging is the only evident cause. Under those criteria, low muscle strength indicates probable sarcopenia, and low muscle quantity or quality confirms the diagnosis.". Reason: The definition presents one diagnostic convention as universal and leaves the boundary between primary and secondary sarcopenia unclear.

goal.need = "In one cohort of 1,420 adults aged 75 or older living in the community, 150 had sarcopenia and 85 of them had low physical performance. Exercise can improve strength and function, but some people cannot take part or gain too little benefit. Nutritional supplements have inconsistent effects. A medicine that preserves mobility could help people keep walking across a room or rising from a chair unaided. Gaining lean body mass alone does not establish that benefit.". Reason: The existing text recounts one trial but omits how many older adults are affected, which daily activities are at stake and who needs another treatment option.

add statement by US Food and Drug Administration, 2017: "advancing the development of safe and effective treatment options for managing sarcopenia". Reason: FDA’s final patient-focused drug development report explicitly endorses developing safe and effective treatments for sarcopenia.

add statement by International Conference on Frailty and Sarcopenia Research Task Force, 2022: "pharmacological agents are needed for people who do not respond to lifestyle modifications". Reason: The international task force explicitly identifies patients for whom a pharmacological treatment is needed.
